relevance_note: This is a 1,000-family exome cohort whose only TNFAIP3 mention is an aggregate count among reanalysis upgrades ('BRIP1 (n = 1), and TNFAIP3 (n = 1)'), with no patient label, variant description, demographics or phenotype, so no individual-level record can be extracted.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown manually; no script transcribed any table (the only table, Table 1, is cohort-level demographics). The single TNFAIP3 mention (Results, Reanalyses) says one case's molecular diagnosis came from upward reclassification of a variant involving TNFAIP3; no variant string, zygosity, inheritance, sex, age or clinical feature is given for that person, and the paper never mentions A20 or haploinsufficiency. Figure 1, Tables E1-E4 and the Online Repository are not in the Markdown (titles only) and may list this TNFAIP3 variant and possibly other TNFAIP3 diagnoses from the initial analysis; n_patients_reported = 1 is therefore only the count the text states (reanalysis subset) and may be a lower bound. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = true concerns cohort participants in SASH3 (ref 20), NCKAP1L (ref 22) and PIK3CG (ref 23) gene-discovery papers, not the TNFAIP3 case, which the paper does not say was reported before. Internal inconsistency: the reanalysis section reports 22 new molecular diagnoses (22/361; 9/22 from new gene-disease associations) but then uses a denominator of 21 for the other categories, including the TNFAIP3 sentence ('contributing 5/21 (23.8%) cases').
